_meta: A small training set drawn from a linear truth with noise, plus separate test points from the same truth, used to show why a model must be judged on held-out data it did not see, not on the data it was fit to. A flexible enough model can drive its error on the training set to zero by bending to pass through every point -- but the training points are the true signal plus noise, so a model that fits them exactly has fit the noise, memorizing quirks that will not recur. Its training error is then a wildly optimistic estimate of how it will do on new data: near zero in-sample, large out-of-sample. A simpler model that cannot bend to every point has a larger training error but captures the signal rather than the noise, so its test error is close to its training error and far below the flexible model's test error. Judging by training error crowns the memorizer; only judging on held-out test points -- data from the same process the model never saw during fitting -- reveals which model actually generalizes. train_x and train_y are the (noisy) training points; test_x and test_true are new inputs and their true (noiseless) targets from the same y = slope*x line. These are the fixture; a flexible memorizer model and a simple least-squares line are each scored on the training set and the test set, and their train-vs-test error gaps are computed.
